system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our side. Its structure is to collapse every protection into a single, low, short general regime (20% cap, high thresholds, 18 months), then extend that regime to title, capacity, tax, IP, fraud and the specific indemnity, while simultaneously (a) widening deemed disclosure to the whole data room and public registers and (b) adding a blanket buyer-knowledge bar. The result would leave us with very limited practical recourse on the matters our own DD has flagged as live (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005, DD-006).

Notably, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update: it confirms that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment evidence and the DD-005 funds-flow treatment are all **not** in place. We should use the Disclosure Letter's own admissions against the Update's "addressed/adequate/settled" characterisations.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General warranty cap – cl 12.1
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **None has been given.**
- **Analysis:** We cannot accept this draft at 20%. Even if we ultimately move, it should be traded for concessions elsewhere (thresholds, period, fundamental carve-outs), not given up on the first turn. Note also that the cap is meaningless if the Seller succeeds in sweeping title, tax, IP and the Ironquay indemnity underneath it (see 2.4–2.5).
- **Position:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Record internally that any 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost's written sign-off referencing this specific draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).

### 2.2 Thresholds – cl 12.2
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** (deductible) recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the basket has been converted from a tipping basket to a true deductible. Together they would wipe out the first AUD 250,000 of loss entirely and exclude any individual claim under AUD 25,000 regardless of aggregate, which is a serious gap for a business with multiple mid-sized contractual exposures (e.g. Sandbar renewals at AUD 110,000 each would each clear the de minimis but could be eaten by the basket).
- **Position:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. Expressly state that Fundamental/Title claims, Tax claims, specific indemnities and fraud are outside both thresholds.

### 2.3 Time limits and the "applies to all Claims" clause – cl 12.3 / 13
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims, plus a proposal that **any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise**.
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Separate categories must be kept distinct; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Analysis:** The 18 months is a straightforward departure. The second sentence is the more dangerous one: it is a default-rule override that quietly applies the 18-month period (and, read with 12.1/12.2, the cap and thresholds) to Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnity claims unless we remember to carve each one out. This inverts the drafting burden and is exactly the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
- **Position:** 24 months for general claims. **Delete** the "applies to all Claims" default. Replace with an express statement that the general regime in cl 12 applies only to General Warranty Claims and that Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment/covenant and specific indemnity claims are governed solely by their own provisions.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% cap (i.e. price); at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** Unacceptable. If the Seller does not actually own and deliver 100% of the shares, our loss is the entire purchase price, not 20% of it, and the defect may not surface within 18 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. This is one of the two or three points on which we should be prepared to hold firm regardless of other trades.
- **Position:** Reinstate a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime: cap at AUD 24,000,000, claims period not less than six years, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier, no reliance on disclosure.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; this is a non-waivable instruction.
- **Analysis:** As drafted there is **no fraud carve-out at all**. "All Claims of any nature" would purport to cap and time-bar claims for fraud and would have the non-reliance clause operate as a shield against fraudulent pre-contractual statements. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, such a clause is of doubtful enforceability in respect of fraud, but we should not rely on a court to fix the drafting. It would also sweep the Ironquay indemnity and payment covenants (price, Riverlark, bonuses) into the warranty cap.
- **Position:** Insert an express carve-out: nothing in cl 9, 12, 13 or 20 limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its officers/advisers. Confirm that exclusive-remedy and non-reliance do not apply to Fundamental Warranties, Tax, specific indemnities or payment obligations. We should not accept any dilution of this point in later turns.

### 2.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2]
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** Paragraph [1.1] is whole-data-room deemed disclosure; [1.2] adds public registers. Combined with cl 8.3 (below), the Seller would be disclosed against every warranty to the extent any document anywhere in the room could be said to "refer to" a matter, whether or not a reasonable buyer would have identified the problem from it. The specific disclosures in sections 2–10 are actually quite narrow and heavily hedged ("does not state whether…"), so the general disclosure is doing most of the work. Paragraph [1.4] (no admission of anything) further undermines the utility of the specific disclosures as a basis for pricing.
- **Position:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2]. Replace with a fair-disclosure standard: a matter is disclosed only if fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents are disclosed only where specifically cross-referenced against a specific warranty. No public register deemed disclosure. Delete or confine [1.4] so it does not neutralise the specific disclosures.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge – cl 8.3
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals (and seller knowledge qualifiers to named seller persons after reasonable enquiry); never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable". It overlaps with 2.6 to produce a near-total exclusion: anything in the room is deemed disclosed, and anything discoverable from the room is deemed known. It would also, on its face, bar the Ironquay indemnity (we clearly "know" about DD-004/DD-010) and any claim on the DD-006 incident, both of which are precisely the matters we have negotiated specific protection for.
- **Position:** Delete cl 8.3. If the Seller insists on some knowledge concept, confine it to actual knowledge of a short list of named Buyer deal team individuals, exclude advisers, exclude anything "discoverable", and expressly exclude Fundamental Warranties, fraud, Tax and all specific indemnities from its operation.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3
- **Seller:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter s.2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%); consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions under cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of conditions** is in the room.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Analysis:** The Update's "addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. A consent that is conditional under cl 11.3 is not an effective consent until the conditions are met; "satisfied on delivery" would let the Seller complete on a piece of paper whose conditions may later fail, leaving us holding 30% revenue risk. Reasonable endeavours is too soft for a condition of this materiality.
- **Position:** Condition precedent: delivery of an unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or a conditional consent together with documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen), in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer, in each case before Completion. Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours", with a positive obligation to procure, and a Buyer right not to complete if not satisfied. Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment mechanism for Bluefen termination within an agreed post-Completion window if the Seller will not give an unconditional CP.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Disclosure Letter s.3:** facility not repaid; no final discharge of security included; change-of-control at cl 8.1.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still outstanding and only a promise of a future release is inconsistent with the price basis and leaves the target's assets encumbered in our hands. It also triggers the cl 8.1 change-of-control. A post-Completion release is not within the deal team's authority to accept.
- **Position:** Completion deliverables to include (i) a Riverlark payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion, (ii) direction for the payout amount to be paid directly from Completion funds to Riverlark, (iii) executed releases/discharges of all security (including PPSR discharge forms) and any required change-of-control consent or waiver, delivered against payment. If the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion, the fallback is an irrevocable, unconditional bank undertaking to release on receipt of funds, and only with Amelia Frost's written approval.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses / funds flow – DD-005
- **Seller:** bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure Letter s.5:** conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not** in the draft funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific funds-flow line item or demonstrably Seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Analysis:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company. If they are not funded through the flow or deducted as Debt/transaction expenses, we would inherit AUD 420,000 plus on-costs post-Completion, contrary to the debt-free/cash-free basis. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually pays them; the draft does not say so. The on-cost position is undetermined on the material; we should not assume a figure, but we should require it to be quantified and covered.
- **Position:** Require the DD-005 bonuses and all associated on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any employer contributions) to be either (a) a specific line in the funds flow paid from the Seller's proceeds at Completion, or (b) treated as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the price adjustment, or (c) covered by a specific Seller indemnity with set-off rights. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost treatment and quantum before signing.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP – cl 11.1
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Disclosure Letter s.4:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independent bank verification; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Analysis:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 payment; it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials has not passed, so the Company may not own IP it uses or has delivered to customers. An indemnity confined to the payment does not cover infringement claims, re-development cost, customer claims or loss of exclusivity. The Seller's own letter confirms there is no confirmatory assignment. We should not assume AUD 180,000 is the correct exposure in either direction.
- **Position:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to pay all outstanding SOW3 fees and procure from Ironquay a written receipt plus a confirmatory assignment of all SOW3 Project Materials to the Company (preserving the cl 7.3 cure path); (ii) broaden cl 11.1 to an indemnity covering all losses arising from the Company not holding good title to the SOW3 (and any other Ironquay) deliverables, including third-party claims and remediation cost, outside the general cap/basket/time limits and not subject to cl 8.3 or disclosure; (iii) if the amount remains disputed, escrow or retention of an amount to be agreed once verified.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident – cl 4.6 / Sch 6 / DD-006
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Disclosure Letter s.6:** download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification requirement not determined; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Analysis:** We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation nor overstate it. The honest position is that the facts are unresolved. What matters contractually is that the Seller does not use the general disclosure (s.6) and cl 8.3 to disclose the entire incident against the privacy/data warranties and then cap the residual exposure at the general regime.
- **Position:** (i) Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and link-access records; complete the investigation with a written report to the Buyer before Completion; notify the Buyer of any development and any decision on regulator/individual notification; (ii) a specific indemnity for losses arising from the DD-006 incident (including notification, regulatory and third-party costs) outside the general regime and unaffected by disclosure or buyer knowledge; (iii) no numeric claim or price adjustment is made at this stage.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals – DD-008 / DD-011
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure Letter s.8:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure, but the playbook does not direct us to treat these as Debt. The information gap is the issue.
- **Position:** Request the renewal documents, notice/termination provisions, accrual status and timing relative to the Locked Box/Completion date. Decide treatment (ordinary course vs. Debt/leakage) once reviewed. In the meantime, ensure the warranties on material contracts and the no-leakage/ordinary-course covenant are not disclosed against by the general disclosure.

### 2.14 Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Seller:** tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime.
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; keep categories separate; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Analysis:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller is attempting to close an open point by assertion and to fold Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime. Tax in particular conventionally sits on a longer period (aligned with assessment periods) and often a separate cap.
- **Position:** Reply that Tax and IP remain open and are not governed by cl 12 unless and until separately agreed. Do not counter with a specific tax cap/period in this turn beyond stating they will be separate; we do not assert unlimited liability.

### 2.15 Title evidence – DD-012
- **Seller:** title to 100% is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Disclosure Letter s.10:** DD-012 is the source relied on; it does not state that the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Analysis:** A company's own register, supplied by the Seller, is an assertion by the Seller. We need independent corroboration before Completion.
- **Position:** Completion deliverables / pre-Completion checks: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller for charges over the shares; copies of share certificates (or confirmation none issued) and instruments of transfer; board/shareholder resolutions and constitutional authority for the Seller to sell; confirmation of no options, pre-emption rights or shareholder agreements; and Fundamental Warranties on title and encumbrances backed by the 100% / six-year regime in 2.4.

### 2.16 Minor points
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification only on the Seller's account. Confirm the clause ourselves; if correct, make Completion notification a Seller deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment, not change of control. Confirm by reading the clause; if correct, no CP required.

## 3. Interaction effects to emphasise in our response

The individual points above compound. If the Seller got cl 8.3 (constructive knowledge), Sch 7 [1.1]–[1.2] (whole-room disclosure), the "applies to all Claims" default, and the extension of 9.3/12.8/20.5 to "all Claims", then in practice:

- every DD-flagged matter would be disclosed and "known", so the warranties would be unavailable for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005, DD-006 and Sandbar;
- the Ironquay indemnity and any DD-006 indemnity would be capped at 20% and barred after 18 months and possibly defeated by cl 8.3;
- title failure would be capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse; and
- fraud would purportedly be capped and time-barred.

We should make the structural point to the Seller once, clearly, rather than arguing each clause in isolation.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|-------|-----------------|--------------|
| 1 | Cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m. No authority exists for 20%. |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar. |
| 3 | Period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months. No authority exists for 18. |
| 4 | "All limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | Delete. Each category governed only by its own regime. |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. |
| 6 | 9.3/12.8/20.5 to "all Claims" | No fraud carve-out | Insert fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable. |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL [1.1]–[1.2], [1.4]) | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete general disclosure; confine [1.4]. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete. Any residual qualifier: actual knowledge of named individuals only; never for title, capacity, fraud, Tax or indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: effective consent plus evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion; stronger endeavours obligation. |
| 10 | Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Not in funds flow | Specific line item (plus on-costs) or Seller-funded/indemnified; quantify on-costs before signing. |
| 12 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 payment only | Pre-Completion payment + receipt + confirmatory assignment; broaden indemnity to title/infringement losses outside general regime. AUD 180k unverified. |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Log preservation, completed investigation and reporting pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside general regime. No numeric position. |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Request documents; assess before classifying. No automatic Debt treatment. |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Remain open; separate regimes; not folded into cl 12. |
| 16 | Title (DD-012) | Register only | Independent ASIC/PPSR searches, certificates, transfers, authority evidence; Fundamental Warranty backing. |

**Internal actions:** (a) note on the file that this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update) has **not** received Amelia Frost authority for either the 20% cap or the 18-month period, so neither can be conceded; (b) escalate the Riverlark post-Completion release proposal to Amelia Frost only if the Seller refuses Completion-date releases; (c) instruct DD team to obtain the Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions, the Sandbar renewal terms, the DD-005 on-cost analysis and the independent title searches before the next turn.
=== END ADVICE ===
